diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage infeed starvation or jam at the starwheel likely caused by damaged or fallen containers or misaligned guide rails, leading to a sharp drop in filler speed.
recommended_actions: Inspect the starwheel area for any jammed or damaged containers.
Check guide rails for proper adjustment and wear.
Verify upstream depalletizer operation to ensure it is running.
Clear any blockages and resume operation cautiously.
sources: conveyor_system.md#Error code E-402: Infeed starvation / jam

diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage main drive bearing wear or lack of lubrication causing increasing vibration.
recommended_actions: Inspect main drive bearings for wear or lubrication issues.
Check drive coupling alignment.
Verify mounting bolts are tight.
Monitor vibration levels closely for further increase.

diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage product temperature rise likely due to glycol pump failure or refrigerant issue in the chiller system, as temperature is steadily increasing and projected to exceed 5 C soon, matching symptoms of E-214 before alarm triggers.
recommended_actions: Inspect glycol pump operation and seals for leaks or failure.
Check refrigerant levels and compressor status in the chiller system.
Clean or inspect plate heat exchanger for fouling if pump and refrigerant are normal.
Monitor temperature closely to confirm if it continues rising towards alarm threshold.
diagnosis.spare_part: GP-220 seal kit (if glycol pump seal leak confirmed)
sources: chiller_system.md#Error code E-214: Product temperature high

diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage CO2 pressure drop likely due to a leak at a CO2 line fitting or regulator diaphragm issue.
recommended_actions: Check bulk CO2 tank level to ensure it is not running low.
Perform leak test on CO2 line fittings using soapy water; tighten or replace any leaking fittings.
If pressure continues to drift after tightening fittings, replace the regulator diaphragm.
sources: carbonation_co2.md#Error code E-118: CO2 pressure low

diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage product chiller system fault likely due to low refrigerant, compressor trip, glycol pump failure, or fouled plate heat exchanger causing rising product temperature.
recommended_actions: Inspect chiller refrigerant levels and compressor status.
Check glycol pump operation and seals for leaks.
Examine plate heat exchanger for fouling or blockage.
Monitor temperature trend closely to prevent product quality issues.
sources: chiller_system.md#Error code E-214: Product temperature high

diagnosis.root_cause: Early-stage infeed starvation or jam likely due to containers or guide rails issues causing filler speed to drop.
recommended_actions: Inspect starwheel and guide rails for jams or damage.
Check conveyor chain condition and alignment.
Verify upstream depalletizer operation.
sources: conveyor_system.md#Error code E-402: Infeed starvation / jam
